To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the optimum post-combiners are FIR filters whose transfer functions are closely related to the transfer functions of the prototype filter in the CMFB, (2) the number of adaptive coefficients in the optimum post-combines is one third of those reported in earlier work, and (3) the convergence behavior of the least mean-square (LMS) adaptation of the post-combines can be characterized by a single parameter, the largest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix of the input signal.

the optimum post-combiners for cosine-modulated filterbanks are finite impulse response (IIR) filters with a number of taps equal to the number of subcarriers, the optimum transfer functions of these post-combiner are related to the prototype filters in cosine modulation and demodulations blocks, and the LMS algorithm used for adaptation of post-combiners has no slow mode of convergences.
the optimum post-combiners are finite impulse response filters whose coefficients are related to those of the prototype filter in the CMFB analysis and synthesize blocks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and design of post-combiners for CMFB-based transmultiplexers.
the analysis and design of the post-combining equalizer in CMFB-based transmultiplexer system.
the development of efficient post-combiner structures for use in CMFB-based MCM systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the post-combiners used in cosine modulated-based transmultiplexers are FIR and closely related to prototype filter of the CMFB analysis and synthesizer blocks.
the post-combiners used in the cosine-modulated-based MCM systems can be designed in such a way that they have FIR structures and can be adapted by a fast LMS algorithm.
the proposed post-combiner is a good choice for use in MCM applications that use CMFBs for modulation and demodulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new structure of post-combiners in CMFB-based transmultiplexer and MCM systems that has about one third the number of adaptive coefficients of the earlier structures.
the post-combiners used in cosine-modulated transmultiplexers can be implemented as FIR filters with the number of taps equal to the number of subcarriers in the transmultiplexer.
we have developed a simple post-combiner design that is computationally efficient and that has fast convergence rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by making a reasonable assumption, we are able to obtain closed form equations for optimum post combiner transfer functions, and by using these equations we can design an efficient and robust post-combiner.
the post-combiners can be implemented as FIR filters with a small number of taps.
the post-combiners used in cosine-modulated transmultiplexer systems are FIR filters and can be easily implemented using the fast Fourier transform (FFT).
